title: Hosted Endpoint Slim Specs & Canary Ops Playbook
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: This ticket captures a focused PRD for a minimal, launchable hosted inference surface covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints plus an operational canary and rollback playbook. The goal is to ship a slim, well-instrumented endpoint set that meets behavior and cost guardrails for self-serve customers and signal the readiness criteria for Dedicated/Private offers. This PRD emphasizes deterministic behavioral contracts for common consumer patterns, measurable telemetry, and a staged canary with explicit abort conditions.
objectives: Define a minimal behavioral contract for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank that supports 90% of current usage patterns while reducing implementation complexity.
Ensure production operability: end-to-end telemetry, per-route cost telemetry, and a documented canary/rollback procedure that product and on-call can execute without infra changes.
Gate launch on objective metrics: latency SLOs, quality regression thresholds, and unit-cost guardrails for common traffic slices.
non_goals: Do not include multi-model orchestration or complex A/B experiment frameworks in MVP; those are future work for Dedicated feature set.
No new SDK surface changes — use existing API formats and surface-contracts unless a backward-incompatible bug is discovered.
No large-scale migration tooling for older tenant configurations in this sprint.
scope_clarifications: Chat: provide single-turn and multi-turn with explicit conversation token limits; system/user/function call semantics follow existing hosted behavior.
Completions: support both synchronous and streaming output; capped at configured max tokens per request.
Embeddings: produce consistent dimensionality across model families; surface a per-request deterministic seed behavior for reproducible indexing.
Rerank: expose a lightweight candidate scoring endpoint that accepts precomputed embeddings and returns ranked IDs with scores.
Fallbacks: where a requested model variant is unavailable, automatically fallback to a pre-specified compatible variant; behavior documented in response metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral correctness: 95% of sampled prompts from the production probe set return within expected label buckets for content/format (per eval harness).
Latency: p95 generation latency for 64-token completions <= 150ms in the primary region under nominal load profile (per telemetry).
Cost unit: for a representative micro-benchmark suite, average cost-per-token (hosted infra) for the slimline models must be <= 0.85x current baseline for the same quality band.

Quality regression protection: automatic evals comparing baseline and release commit must show no >2% absolute drop in rerank recall@10 and no >1.5% drop in embedding retrieval mean-reciprocal-rank on seeded datasets.
Operational readiness: dashboards for per-route error rate, p95 latency, token throughput, and cost-per-token must be live and linked in the runbook prior to canary start.
Canary abort rules: abort if error rate > 2x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes, or p95 latency increases by >50% over baseline for 5 minutes, or eval quality regressions exceed thresholds.
rollout_strategy: Phase 0: Internal smoke — dev + SE tenants only; quick sanity checks on requests and metrics (1 hour).
Phase 1: Canary — 1% of production traffic to slimline endpoints with weighted routing; run for 6 hours of production window, monitor metrics and automated evals.
Phase 2: Ramp — incrementally increase traffic if no aborts; 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over multiple controlled deploys and business-day monitoring.
Rollback: immediate route reweight to previous stable model variant and a deploy rollback if abort rules are hit; documented rapid-runbook steps for SRE and PM.
launch_checklist: PRD reviewed and approved by Eng, Design, Security, and SRE leads.
Open-source-style behavioral contract doc published to internal confluence with example payloads for each endpoint.
Implementation PRs merged with integration tests and canary routing flags guarded behind a feature toggle.
Telemetry: dashboards and alerts created and smoke-tested; query templates for investigative debugging documented.
Canary & rollback playbook added to on-call runbook and communicated in the weekly SRE rotation handoff.
Docs: public API reference updated, quickstart examples validated, and SDK compatibility smoke-tested.
Legal/Security: security checklist signed off and key customer-facing privacy notes validated.
Stakeholder signoff meeting scheduled with SVP Product and one customer success engineer for go/no-go.
